subject: Clarifying buying paths: Cloud marketplace vs direct contract — procurement checklist
messages:
From: Ava Simmons <procurement@finedge-payments.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@finedge-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood purchasing route questions (Marketplace vs Direct)

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well. We’re finalizing our procurement path for the pilot and had a few concrete questions that will determine whether we buy through AWS Marketplace (SaaS listing) or pursue a direct Redwood contract. Can you confirm the following?

1) Invoicing & billing cadence: If we purchase via AWS Marketplace, will Redwood still be able to provide consolidated monthly invoices that align with our internal cost center mapping? If not, what’s the expected timing to receive invoice-level details?
2) Co-sell and discounts: Is the co-sell discount applied on Marketplace line items, or do we need a separate reseller/partner setup to capture the discount agreed in our discussions with your AE?
3) Term & entitlements: Marketplace listings sometimes lock term to Marketplace billing. If we start on Marketplace, can we later migrate to a direct contract without service interruption? Any implications for data residency or audit logs?
4) Procurement timeline: Our legal/procurement prefers Marketplace for faster PO acceptance, but they need confirmation about SLA credits and exportable audit logs (for PCI) before signing.

We’d appreciate a short checklist we can share with procurement to reconcile internal steps vs vendor-side steps. Attaching our internal requirements doc. Can someone from your side send a one-pager we can hand to our procurement/legal team?

Thanks,
Ava Simmons
Procurement Lead | FinEdge Payments
procurement@finedge-payments.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Finedge_MultiRegion_requirements_v1.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Simmons <procurement@finedge-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@finedge-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood purchasing route questions (Marketplace vs Direct)

Ava — thanks for the clear list. I’ve put together a practical checklist below (we’ll also attach a one-page that you can hand off). Quick answers first, then the checklist: 

- Invoicing & billing cadence: Marketplace billing is handled via AWS and will appear on your AWS invoice. We can provide monthly usage exports and per-invoice line-item breakdowns in CSV form within 48 hours of month close for reconciliation. If you need Redwood-branded consolidated invoices, that requires a direct contract.
- Co-sell and discounts: Co-sell incentives typically flow through partner programs and require registration of the opportunity in the partner portal. A Marketplace purchase can be eligible for co-sell, but to apply negotiated enterprise discounts (custom pricing) we need a direct purchase path (or a marketplace private offer from our side).
- Term & entitlements: You can start on Marketplace and migrate to a direct contract. We support model-pin continuity and will migrate subscription entitlements without disruption if planned ahead (we recommend a 7–10 day cutover window for billing reconciliation). Exportable audit logs and data residency choices are available regardless of buying path — the control plane for Private/Dedicated differs but audit exports are available in both.
- SLA credits / compliance: SLA credits are available under both routes, but Marketplace SLA claims need to be filed via AWS Marketplace support (we’ll assist). For PCI/regulated audits, we provide the same audit log exports; evidence collection may be faster on a direct contract because we can provide additional attestation and a named contact for auditors.

Procurement checklist (one-pager summary):
- Decide target buying path: Marketplace (fastest PO acceptance) vs Direct (custom pricing, branded invoices, named support).
- If Marketplace: request private offer from Redwood (we’ll generate), confirm marketplace private offer terms, notify us of marketplace order id, share AWS invoice contacts for CSV exports.
- If Direct: request SOW & commercial terms, sign direct MSA, provide billing contact.
- Co-sell / discount: if wanting AE-negotiated discounts, request a private offer or direct contract. Register opportunity in partner portal (we’ll provide next steps).
- Data & compliance: confirm required audit exports (we’ll deliver logs and SOC2 report). If you need on-prem or VPC, that’s under Private deployment and requires additional procurement steps.
- Cutover plan: 7–10 day billing reconciliation, confirm effective date and that API keys will be rotated during migration.

I’ve attached two files: a quick one-pager for procurement and an initial Marketplace quote for the pilot (spreadsheet). Laura — flag anything I missed on the enterprise/partner ops side.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 650-555-0199

Attachments: Redwood_AWS_Marketplace-quote.xlsx; Redwood_Marketplace_and_Direct_onepager.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Simmons <procurement@finedge-payments.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@finedge-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood purchasing route questions (Marketplace vs Direct)

Thanks Rishi — this covers the core items. Two operational addenda from Partner Ops / Billing: 

1) Marketplace private offer vs public listing: For the negotiated discount we discussed, we’ll issue a Marketplace Private Offer tied to FinEdge’s AWS account. That allows your procurement to process via Marketplace while preserving our negotiated price and co-sell credit. Action: Marco — please share your AWS account ID and the person who will accept the private offer.

2) Invoice reconciliation & cost centers: If you need line-item mapping to your internal cost centers, we’ll include a tokenized cost-center field in the CSV export. For direct contracts we can also generate a Redwood invoice with those mappings for your AP team.

I’ve added the standard cutover checklist below as a short sequence you can paste into a PO: 
- Accept Marketplace Private Offer (if chosen) or sign Direct MSA and SOW.
- Provide billing contact and AWS account id (if Marketplace).
- Receive marketplace order id / Redwood invoice id.
- Validate first month CSV export and close reconciliation window (7–10 days).

If FinEdge would like, Marissa on our team can run a 30-min intake with your procurement to walk them through the private offer acceptance flow and the CSV sample.

Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_Direct_SOW_template.pdf

Laura / Rishi — helpful, thank you. Procurement prefers Marketplace for speed but wants the negotiated pricing in place.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll send AWS account ID and the acceptance user by EOD.
- Please prepare a Marketplace Private Offer (with the agreed pilot pricing and co-sell registration steps) and a DocuSign copy of the (short) SOW for internal sign-off.
- We’ll need the sample CSV export format and one month of historical usage export for our finance team to validate the mapping.

Ava will coordinate PO issuance once the private offer and DocuSign SOW are ready. Thanks Marissa for the intake offer — we’ll take the 30-min walkthrough.

Onward,
